messages:
emily: Hey team — just installed redwoodctl via brew and hit three things: postinstall auto-update failed, zsh completion didn't install, and my old ~/.redwood profiles were migrated twice (profile and profile-1). Anyone seen this combo?

nora: what errors did you get?

emily: paste:
```
==> Running post-install hooks
/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl update-self --background
Error: permission denied writing /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/1.2.0/_update/state.json
Warning: completion install failed: mkdir /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions: permission denied
Migrating old profiles from ~/.redwood to ~/.config/redwood
wrote ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json
wrote ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json (profile-1)
```

chao: sounds like brew ran as root for the package path so user can't write. That would also explain the migration running twice if the first write failed mid-rename.

emily: yep `ls -ld /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl` shows root:admin.

nora: quick fixes: chown just the redwoodctl paths, then run `brew postinstall redwoodctl`. For zsh completion: `redwoodctl completion zsh | sudo tee /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_redwoodctl`.

emily: done and autoupdate completed. login then prompted for keychain repeatedly though. Is there a way to skip macOS keychain?

chao: use `redwoodctl login --no-keychain` if you prefer file-based creds, we'll add that to docs. Also we should make migration atomic (write to temp + rename) and detect EACCES to give a hint about brew perms.

devex-bot: Created issue #701: "mac installer: handle permission errors in postinstall & migration; document --no-keychain and completion install steps" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/701

emily: thanks! filed output and the ls results in the issue. thread resolved for me. :white_check_mark:
